tweets.text:
PM Seeks Tony Blair Institute’s Support for AI, OECD Bid

Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul met former British prime minister Tony Blair on Monday to discuss cooperation with the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change on artificial intelligence, advanced industries, clean energy and public-sector reform.

Anutin sought TBI’s advice on attracting investment in AI, semiconductors and other advanced industries, as well as using AI to raise productivity and improve government services. Blair said Thailand should seek greater control over data hosted in the country and use it to develop locally relevant applications and startups.

The two sides also discussed TBI support for Thailand’s target of joining the OECD by 2028 and agreed to appoint officials to explore practical cooperation on the digital and green transitions. Blair said the institute was willing to advise the government.

Vid via PM's Press Office 

#Thailand #AI #OECD

Role of Satellites in Weather Forecasts

In this fragment of the ALLATRA Podcast, Dr. Stephen M. Volz explains the crucial role satellites play in modern weather forecasting. He discusses how observations from space provide continuous data about the atmosphere and Earth, helping meteorologists and forecasting systems understand current conditions and predict how weather will develop.

In this episode of the ALLATRA Podcast in collaboration with ALLATRA Global Research Center, Dr. Stephen M. Volz shares insights from decades of leadership in NASA and NOAA.

Drawing on his experience, Dr. Volz explains how humanity has transformed its ability to observe Earth and why our planet should be understood not as separate oceans, atmosphere, and land, but as one interconnected system.

The conversation explores how satellite observations become weather forecasts, why climate prediction is far more complex than it seems, how artificial intelligence is reshaping Earth observation, and why human expertise remains irreplaceable. Dr. Volz also discusses the critical role of oceans in Earth's climate system and the future of Earth observation.

tweets.text:
Studio Ghibli has spent decades creating hand-drawn films that people still return to years later.

When AI-generated “Ghibli-style” images flooded the internet, the studio’s longtime producer and co-founder Toshio Suzuki declined every interview request.

He believed people would quickly get bored of the trend.

“And that’s exactly what happened.”

Suzuki says AI can create certain kinds of animation, but anyone with some knowledge can immediately recognize it. To him, it isn’t meaningful or interesting.

According to Suzuki, Hayao Miyazaki doesn’t even know what generative AI is. His creative process remains rooted in his own memories, imagination, and hand-drawn craft.

AI can imitate the surface of Ghibli’s style.

Recreating what makes its films timeless is a much harder problem.
